artworks.title: Morpheus and Iris
artworks.description: An oil by Pierre-Narcisse Guérin showing Iris waking or addressing Morpheus, the shaper of dreams. Neoclassical flesh and cool drapery stage Ovid's dream-messenger as a sleeping youth interrupted by the rainbow goddess — sleep personified at the threshold of waking.

artworks.title: Morpheus (Sleep)
artworks.description: An oil by Jean-Bernard Restout in the Cleveland Museum of Art, exhibited as Morpheus or Sleep. A nude youth sinks into oblivion on dark drapery — the Oneiros who takes human form in dreams reduced to pure, academic repose, the body as the vessel of night.

artworks.title: Aurora Awakening Morpheus
artworks.description: A ceiling or decorative oil by Bartolomeo Altomonte in which Aurora, goddess of dawn, rouses Morpheus from sleep. Light breaks over the dream-god's limbs — the daily contest between daybreak and the architect of dreams, painted for an Austrian Baroque interior.

popCulture.title: Morphine
popCulture.description: The painkiller took Morpheus' name — the dream-shaper as the root of morphine, the drug that brings sleep.

popCulture.title: Morpheus
popCulture.description: Ovid's dream-messenger remains the poetic name for sleep's architect — Morpheus as the face that dreams wear.
